recentItems.title: Treehouses NOW | Pete Nelson | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
I want to inspire people who have always dreamed about building a treehouse to give themselves permission to make it real. These structures have a way of connecting us to nature, to each other, and to something lasting and magical.  Too often, the permitting process or the fear of how to start stops people before they even begin. My message is simple: you can do this. You do not have to build alone. There is a whole community ready to help you along the way. It is about creativity, collaboration, and bringing a little more wonder into the world, one treehouse at a time. Pete Nelson transformed a childhood dream—a simple tree fort built with his father in New Jersey—into a movement that reconnects people with the natural world through pioneering sustainable architecture and elevated living.
As founder of Nelson Treehouse, Pete has redefined what's possible when imagination meets craftsmanship among the branches. His innovative designs have elevated treehouses from childhood playgrounds to sophisticated spaces for living, working, and healing.
Through Animal Planet's "Treehouse Masters," Pete brought elevated living to millions worldwide, inspiring new relationships with nature and evoking childhood nostalgia. His expertise is showcased in six acclaimed books on treehouse design and through his robust social media following, which serve as both practical guides and sources of inspiration.
But Pete's true mission extends far beyond building structures. In a world where we spend most of our time indoors and online, he champions a philosophy that views treehouses as gateways to wonder, mindfulness, and environmental stewardship. Through Nelson Treehouse vacation rentals across the United States and his high-quality treehouse hardware line for DIYers, he empowers others to discover the transformative power of time spent among the canopy.
As treehouse design evolves into a recognized architectural practice, Pete champions a compelling vision: that our path forward leads up into the branches and back to our fundamental connection with the living world.
Join Pete as he explores how ascending into the trees can ground us in what matters most. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Defining balance for the sandwich generation | Isabel Vallejo Echavarría | TEDxThonglor Women
recentItems.description:
What happens when caring for your parents and raising your children become your responsibility at the same time? This talk challenges us to rethink what caregiving really means and how we can create healthier, more human ways to care for the people we love while navigating our own lives. As a systems engineer, business development manager, and digital strategist across three continents, Isabel kept encountering the same puzzle: Why do brilliant people feel inexplicably stuck? After navigating her own journey as an expat mother managing competing priorities across countries and cultures, she discovered the answer: We're anchored by stories about our past that we’ve mistaken for truth.
Now an EMCC Senior Practitioner and founder of Motiva Coaching & Supervision, Isabel specialises in helping driven professionals courageously face their personal history and rewrite it as aprendizajes—transformative wisdom that opens the path to fulfilling relationships and prosperity. Her innovative approach combines neuroscience-backed frameworks like "Energy Economics" and "Boundaries as Bridges" with creative methodologies including LEGO® SERIOUS PLAY® and systemic mediation. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Education Was Built for a World That No Longer Exists | Sanjay Divakar | TEDxThird Ward Salon
recentItems.description:
What if the biggest problem with education isn't AI—but the system that existed long before AI arrived?

In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Sanjay Divakar draws on his experience attending schools across India, Dubai, and the United States to question whether traditional education is preparing students for the world they will actually inherit.

From memorization and following instructions to rigid schedules and standardized measures of success, Sanjay explores how schools have been designed around predictability—even though the future increasingly demands adaptability, creativity, and the ability to ask better questions.

He argues that AI isn't breaking education. It's revealing where education was already broken.

If machines can memorize, calculate, generate, and complete tasks faster than humans, then perhaps the question isn't how we can compete with AI. It's whether we should continue measuring human potential by the same standards in the first place.

Sanjay challenges educators, parents, and students to rethink what school is preparing young people for—and to have the courage to let go of practices that no longer serve them.

The future of education may not require more technology.

It may require us to finally change the way we think. Sanjay Divakar is a student and emerging voice in the conversation about the future of education. Having experienced education systems in India, Dubai, and the United States, he brings a unique cross-cultural perspective to the question of how schools prepare young people for an increasingly unpredictable world.

His experiences navigating different education systems led him to question the assumptions behind traditional schooling, particularly its emphasis on memorization, instruction-following, and standardized measures of achievement.

In his TEDx talk, Sanjay explores the impact of AI on education and makes the case for a system that places greater emphasis on adaptability, curiosity, critical thinking, and asking the right questions. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What a West African Drum Can Teach About Community | Baba Cedrick Ogunrinde | TEDxThird Ward Salon
recentItems.description:
In this TEDx talk, Baba Cedrick invites us to see the djembe not just as an instrument, but as a living model for community. By breaking down its parts, (i.e. the shell, the skin, the rings, and the rope) he reveals a powerful insight he learned from the djembe: strong communities are built through intentional roles, shared tension, and connection. Blending storytelling, cultural wisdom, and live drumming, he challenges us to rethink leadership, honor emerging voices, and understand tension not as a threat, but as the source of harmony. Baba Cedrick (Abiono) Ogunrinde is a master West African drummer, educator, and culture bearer whose work explores rhythm as a pathway to connection, healing, and community. A Djembefola with over three decades of study, he trained under renowned masters including Famadou Konaté, Mamady Keita, and the late Bernard Woma. His musical lineage spans Guinea, Mali, Ghana, and Nigeria, and his artistry has appeared on global stages, from professional dance companies and theater productions to the film Coming 2 America, where he both performed and helped craft authentic African music.



As a teaching artist, Baba Cedrick works with people of all ages through schools, cultural organizations, and experiential workshops. Grounded in ancestral tradition and academic study, his work uses West African drumming and dance as a conduit for emotional, mental, physical, and spiritual healing, reminding us that community, like rhythm, is something we choose to build together. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Voices Unheard: What Rural Communities Teach us | David Chang | TEDxUBC
recentItems.description: What can rural communities teach us about strength, leadership, and care? Drawing on his experiences living across Western Canada, David Chang explores the lessons embedded within rural communities and the important perspectives they offer in an increasingly changing world. His talk invites us to reconsider the value of community, connection, and the places that shape us. David Chang is a second-year medical student at the University of British Columbia. He grew up across Western Canada, spending time in Alberta, the Interior, Vancouver Island, and now the Lower Mainland. He completed his undergraduate studies in Biology at the University of Victoria and has interests in rural medicine, health advocacy, and substance use treatment. Outside of medicine, David enjoys volleyball, rock climbing, and playing the drums. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Inside the Moment You Think, You Decide: Exploring Free Will | Kia Bahari | TEDxUBC
recentItems.description:
Have you ever made a decision and felt completely certain that you chose it? What if your brain had already begun making that decision before you were even aware of it?

In his talk, Kia Bahari explores the intersection of neuroscience and philosophy to examine one of humanity’s oldest questions: do we really have free will? By looking at what brain science can tell us about how decisions are made, he invites us to reconsider our assumptions about choice, responsibility, and what it means to be human. Kia Bahari is a medical student at UBC, educator, and content creator with a passion for making complex ideas accessible. He is the founder of his own tutoring company and educational YouTube platform, where he helps students navigate challenging university coursework and prepare for the MCAT. His interests span medicine, neuroscience, education, and the questions that emerge at the intersection of science and philosophy. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Winning Isn’t Everything — Growing Is | Sasath Pasandul Vitharana | TEDxKandy
recentItems.description:
What if losing a match could be just as valuable as winning one?
For many young athletes, sports can feel like they are all about the scoreboard, medals, trophies, and being the best. But sport teaches us something much bigger than how to win. It teaches us how to grow.
In this talk, 12-year-old Sasath explores the idea that winning is not the only measure of success. Every training session, every mistake, every defeat, and every challenge is an opportunity to become stronger, more disciplined, and more confident.
Through the world of sports, Sasath shares how losing can teach resilience, competition can teach respect, practice can build discipline, and setbacks can help us discover what we are capable of achieving.
The final score tells us who won the game—but it does not tell the whole story.
The real victory is in becoming a better version of yourself than you were yesterday. V. P. Sasath Pasandul Vitharana is a 12-year-old student of Trinity College, Kandy, with a passion for sports, music, and personal development.

An enthusiastic sports lover, Sasath believes that **sports are more than competition—they are a powerful way to develop discipline, perseverance, teamwork, responsibility, and self-confidence. Through his TEDx talk, Sports and Discipline, he explores how the habits developed through sports can shape young people both on and off the field.

Beyond sports, Sasath has a strong love for  music and guitar , using music as another avenue for creativity, expression, and learning. His interests reflect his belief that young people can grow by balancing physical activity, creativity, education, and discipline.

At just 12 years old, Sasath brings a youthful perspective to an important idea:  discipline is not simply about following rules—it is about building the habits that help us become the people we want to be. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: A Language Words Can't Speak | Chahir Mansour | TEDxCairo University
recentItems.description: Before we ever learn to speak, we learn to listen. Music has always been one of humanity's oldest and most universal forms of expression, capable of communicating emotions that words often fail to capture. In this talk, Chahir explores how music transcends language, culture, and background, becoming a shared human experience that connects us all. More than just an art form, music is an invitation to create, to belong, and to express who we are.  Chahir Mansour is a professional drummer and the band manager of Stage 5. A recent Finance & Investment graduate from the Georgia State University, Cairo University joint program, Chahir has balanced his academic journey with a deep passion for music. Having managed and performed in more than 14 concerts across Egypt, he brings firsthand insight into the country's growing music scene and believes in the power of music to connect people beyond words. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Forest Tiger VS Email:Which is worse for your brain? | Dr. Mohamed ElShorbagy | TEDxCairo University
recentItems.description: Stress has become one of the defining emotions of modern life. We spend so much time trying to avoid it, suppress it, or escape it, but what if we've been asking the wrong question all along? In this talk, Dr. Mohamed challenges the way we think about stress by exploring why it exists in the first place. Blending psychology, neuroscience, and biology, he unpacks how stress shapes not only our thoughts and decisions, but also the way our bodies function, from the brain to the body's physiological responses. Dr. Mohamed ElShorbagy is a medical doctor, science communicator, and content creator dedicated to making science accessible to everyone. Believing that knowledge should challenge misconceptions rather than reinforce them, he founded ما وراء النضارة, a platform that simplifies complex scientific concepts and debunks common myths. His work has gained regional and international recognition, including being a FameLab finalist by the British Council and winning the Best Climate Content Creator award in the TikTok MENA Creator Hub competition. He has led workshops during British Science Week and contributed to developing and reviewing scientific content for educational programs under the Egyptian Ministry of Education. Through his work, Dr. ElShorbagy continues to bridge the gap between science and everyday life, inspiring curiosity, critical thinking, and evidence-based understanding. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Battle of Opposites | Doha Abdallah | TEDxCairo University
recentItems.description: Can too much of a good thing become harmful? And can what we fear the most eventually become our greatest strength? Drawing on Carl Jung's concept of Enantiodromia; the idea that everything, when pushed to its extreme, transforms into its opposite, Doha explores the delicate balance that shapes both individuals and civilizations. Through a fascinating blend of geology, Egyptology, ancient history, philosophy, and personal reflection, her talk reveals how nature, history, and even our own lives are governed by the same timeless pattern: every extreme carries the seed of its opposite. Doha Abdallah is a licensed tour guide and a graduate of the Faculty of Tourism Guidance, where she graduated top of her class with academic excellence. Passionate about Egyptology, she is known for bringing Ancient Egypt to life through its everyday stories, correcting common misconceptions, and uncovering lesser-known insights that deepen our understanding of one of history's greatest civilizations. Her work also extends to education, having contributed to The Inclusive Training Playbook for Higher Education through her chapter, Engage, Include, and Interrupt, where she explores how Egyptology can become more engaging, inclusive, and humancentered in both guided tours and academic spaces. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Proof Over Potential | Norhan Nada | TEDxCairo University
recentItems.description: What if your greatest obstacle isn't failure, but your own potential? We're often taught that being "full of potential" is something to be proud of. But what happens when potential becomes a place we hide? In this talk, Norhan explores the subtle trap of endless preparation, self-improvement, and waiting for the "right time." Through personal experiences and hard-earned lessons, she challenges the audience to stop treating potential as an identity and start turning it into action. Because the greatest loss isn't failing, it's never discovering what you're truly capable of. Norhan Nada is a Computer Engineering student at Cairo University, a technology enthusiast, and a public speaker passionate about innovation and personal growth. Her journey has taken her from winning Red Bull Basement Egypt to reaching the global Top 10 in Tokyo, claiming first place at the GEM Hackathon, and representing Egypt at international conferences in Serbia and Turkey. She also participated in the Youth Diplomacy Program by the Egyptian Ministry of Youth and Sports. Having experienced firsthand the gap between endless preparation and meaningful action, Norhan is driven by a simple mission: to help others stop waiting to become extraordinary and start building extraordinary lives. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
